git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Make the capture health check survive a split stdout read

The first real dictation on the new recorder captured perfectly -- 101
chunks holding 100.20s of audio over a 100s wall clock, every chunk exactly
1.000000s -- but the `recording: captured ...` line never appeared in the
log, so the health check was silently absent on the very first run it
existed for.

hs.task delivers whatever happens to be in the pipe, so lw-record's final
`CAPTURED 100.199` can arrive split across two streaming callbacks
("CAPTU" + "RED 100.199"), matching neither half. Confirmed by feeding the
halves separately: both yield nil, while matching against a joined tail
recovers 100.199. Reproductions at 8s, 30s and 109s all delivered the line
intact, which is why this only showed up against a real dictation.

Match against a rolling 200-char tail of the recorder's stdout instead of a
single delivery, and fall back to the termination callback's `out` if it
ever lands there. If it is missing anyway, measure the chunks on disk and
log that instead -- the health check going quiet is exactly how the original
~10% capture loss stayed invisible, so it must never log nothing.

Tests: 87 pass. Both new guards verified to fail on their bug by mutation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
